open_questions: A transit at BTJD 1355.14 is consistent with zero depth (33 ppm, -5.5 sigma) - RV mass measurement needed to confirm a planetary companion and rule out a blended eccentric EB

Odd/even difference (diff_sigma 3.934, depth_ratio 2.1) and marginal secondary (snr 7.014, depth_over_dip 0.2683 at phase 0.4791) need folding at period_x2 27.2 d to test for EB; high-resolution imaging to refine centroid is blocked (centroid_all not_run) but field shows nearby stars at 89.9-111.7 arcsec requiring deep eclipses >34%
Depth changes 467 to 1266 ppm between sectors and within SPOC 2-min (p_constant 0.000536) should be resolved with more sectors and consistent depth vetting
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 2.4 Earth-radius flat-bottomed dip every 13.6 days with three consistent transits and no sign the dip is off the target star. The depth looks shallower in one sector and one of four transits is missing, and there is a weak odd-even difference, both typical signatures to re-check in a binary. With the current low numbers a planet is still the best explanation, and a mass measurement will decide.

reasons.why: Planet-sized (2.4 Rearth, rp_over_rstar 0.02858) with flat bottom (shape.v_sigma -2.537) and duration ratio 1.119, positively favouring a transiting companion over a grazing/eclipsing star despite low xgboost planet_rank 0.14

No centroid result available; neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0 and could_cause_within_1px 0 rule out a star inside one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) able to produce the 816.5 ppm dip, and RUWE 0.95 / non_single_star 0 give no Gaia binary flag

One transit is essentially missing (33 ppm vs ~809 ppm mean) - as expected if one dip falls in a near_gap (p_chance 0.1724) - but the three other transits are consistent in folded light curve; variability is not a coherent phase curve (amplitude 69.93 ppm, ratio_to_depth 0.08564)
